newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks finish sharply lower, turnover modest.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks finish sharply lower, turnover modest.

text.p: Tokyo stocks finished sharply lower on Wednesday, battered psychologically by news that a regional bank had said it suspects a former employee misused bank funds, brokers said. Futures-linked selling also depressed the market, they said.
The key Nikkei 225 average tumbled 276.41 points, or 1.32 percent, to 20,681.67. Its December futures fell 250 points to finish at 20,690.
"The market was in a wait-and-see mood, foreign investors were net sellers and then news of financial trouble at a bank emerged to depress the market further," one broker said.
Hino Motors, the second largest percentage loser, slipped 69 yen to 971, with pessimistic earnings overshadowing the merits of a weaker yen.
Canon Inc jumped due to a weak yen, extending its rally into a third day. It added 20 yen to settle at 2,220.
Turnover at the end of the day was a humble 252 million shares, little changed from 258 million on Tuesday.

There were 784 declining issues, 251 advancing issues and 188 which were unchanged. No sectors posted major gains, but the retreaters were led by transport equipment, mining, railway/bus, non-ferrous metals and pulp/paper.

In other indices, the broader TOPIX was 9.92 points or 0.63 percent down at 1,562.88. The Nikkei 300 lost 1.65 points or 0.56 percent to 293.08. The second-section index shed 2.39 points or 0.12 percent to stand at 2,029.77. Turnover was 11.89 million shares, slightly less than 14.2 million on Tuesday.
The weighted average auction price of language school Nova Corp shares, due to register for over-the-counter (OTC) trade on November 12, was 5,980 yen, the Japan Securities Dealers' Association said.
The OTC index was down 4.52 points or 0.30 percent at 1,491.34 in late Tokyo. -- M.Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk
